name: Matteo Ricci
summary: An Italian Jesuit trained in mathematics sails to Goa and Macau, works his way north through Ming China in scholar's robes over eighteen years, and becomes the first European allowed to live in Beijing.

stops.note: Leaves after studying under Christopher Clavius, having asked for the Indies mission.
Studies Portuguese while waiting for the India fleet.
Teaches and is ordained in Cochin in 1580.
Builds a mission house and displays his world map.
Meets the scholar Qu Rukui and adopts the dress of a Confucian literatus.
Writes his treatise on friendship and befriends Ming princes.
First attempt on the southern capital.
Fails to gain an audience and leaves after two months.
Debates Buddhist monks and meets Xu Guangqi.
Detained for months by the eunuch Ma Tang.
Presents clocks to the Wanli emperor, translates Euclid with Xu Guangqi and dies here.

sources.cite: Nicolas Trigault, De Christiana expeditione apud Sinas (1615), trans. Louis J. Gallagher, China in the Sixteenth Century: The Journals of Matthew Ricci, New York 1953
